_about: Tables for science/TECHNOLOGY.md, DISCOVERY.md, JOURNAL.md and PLAN.md: the availability layer, the discovery states, the journal's classifications and entry fields, the separations, and the development plan. Rex (2026-10-29): the journal records everything encountered; discoveries made with the period's equipment before their historical date are Time Anomalies; the limiter is the equipment, never the chemical; the world is ours in a space-time anomaly version. mark: rex | proposed | open.

separations.title: The five separations (nothing is decided by the year)
separations.source: ChatGPT's list (outside AI), which Rex adopted in his own words: the chemistry is not limited by the period; the equipment is the limiter; a discovery out of its time is a time anomaly in the journal.
rows: Scientific existence: does the substance or reaction exist under the simulated conditions?
mercury calx heated gives oxygen: yes, always
Historical availability: could someone in this setting obtain or make it ordinarily?
oxygen was isolated in 1774; nobody in 1700 sells or knows it
Technological accessibility: does the character have the equipment, materials and knowledge?
a burning lens, mercury calx (red precipitate: an apothecary's good) and a jar over water: all makeable in 1700
Execution difficulty: can the character control the process?
steady hands and a clear day
Provenance: what is it, in the world's history?
a real gas, discovered 74 years early: Historical and Time Anomaly

technology.title: The availability layer: how equipment, fuel, power and knowledge reach a place
technology.source: GOODS.md's recipe rule (materials + equipment + band + knowledge, Rex 2026-10-28/29) and its facilities list are the period's technology layer already; this table adds the general fields a world profile needs so another setting is a different profile, not a rewrite.
rows: which catalogue items a place can hold: common (bought), rare (one maker, a city), none (only as a time anomaly)
GOODS facilities list (the still, the forge, the furnace, the chymist's laboratory)
what it takes to make a piece: materials, a trade, a facility (a glassblower for a retort; a founder for a brass pump)
glass from Europe; copper work in the islands; brass instruments from London and Amsterdam makers
charcoal, wood, bagasse, spirit, oil; the sun; wind, water and animal power; later gas, steam, electricity
charcoal and wood everywhere; a water wheel at a mill; no steam (Newcomen 1712 is in the period but not in the islands), no gas, no electricity
who knows the process: common, learned, foreign (GOODS 3f), or nobody yet (the discovery is the player's)
the apothecary and the chymist know the period's preparations; everything after is nobody's
what a place can supply continuously: running water, ice, a gasworks, mains power
water by bucket; ice none (the freezing mixture needs it); the rest none
a tagged piece of equipment, fuel or power source introduced by the story; its catalogue numbers make its processes possible at once, with no change to CHEMISTRY.md
none unless the story adds one
COMBAT 4d provenance (Rex); the story keeper's rows
the whole table as one record per setting (pirate 1700; a modern city; a prehistoric camp; a science-fiction ship)

states.title: Discovery states: from meeting a thing to understanding it
states.source: ChatGPT's four states (outside AI), kept; the keeper adds what moves an entry between them and what the player sees at each. The microbe is the model case: Leeuwenhoek saw animalcules in 1676 and nobody understood them until the 1860s.
columns: What the engine lets you do
rows: it exists and you have met it
a sketch and a provisional name ('an unknown liquid'; 'a red fish with a horn'); observed appearance
use it blindly: eat it, burn it, throw it
you have measured or tested properties
the measure roles present (balance, thermometer, hydrometer, litmus, the taste and smell, a trial by fire); time with the thing
the properties found (boils at the water bath's heat; sinks in water; turns litmus red; the fish bites at dusk)
repeat what worked; predict a little
a match to a known entry: a book, a teacher, a measuring instrument that names it (spectroscope, mass spectrometer), or the period's test (a flame colour, a precipitate)
its name, formula or species, its known uses, the historical entry (JOURNAL 7)
name it in trade and dialogue; look it up; use it in a recipe that calls for it
you know why it does what it does
experiment and theory: the player's own, or a book of a later century (a time anomaly in itself)
the mechanism, the reactions it takes part in, what it does to a body
design new processes with it; teach it (GOODS 3f: knowledge that survives you if written)

classifications.title: Provenance classifications (Rex's time-anomaly labels, extended; not mutually exclusive)
classifications.source: Rex (COMBAT 4d): a time-anomaly tag on things that do not belong to the period, shown on the item screen, never in battle; the world is ours in a space-time-anomaly version with real places and people not literally where or when they were. ChatGPT's set (outside AI) merged with the one already recorded in COMBAT 4d. Labels never change behaviour (Rex).
rows: consistent with the setting's period and place
rum, scurvy, the retort, Brand's phosphorus (1669)
real, but discovered, introduced or met outside its historical timeline (earlier or later)
oxygen isolated in 1700 (historically 1774); a Bunsen burner in a 1700 laboratory; a creature from another century
'first recorded in <year> by <who>; you have it in <game year>'
from an earlier geological period, named
a Triassic reptile; a Devonian fish
from a real tradition's myth or folklore
a kraken, a mermaid, a voodoo loa's gift
the angel's energy, a demon's form
fictional technology or material on speculative science
the Atlantean mecha's power cell; a sci-fi fish (Rex's example)
the engine has no record of the reaction or thing: not impossible, not yet supported
a synthesis the database does not hold
'nothing known; try, and the world will answer what it can'

entry.title: A journal entry's fields (one shape for a chemical, a plant, a fish, a creature, a disease, a tool, a place)
entry.source: ChatGPT's field list (outside AI) merged with Rex's: a blurb of what it does and what it is used for, when it was discovered and by whom. The entry separates what the player found from the historical reference that unlocks on identification; the five historical dates are kept apart because they differ and credit is often disputed.
rows: chemical | element | mineral | plant | fungus | animal | fish | creature | disease | equipment | material | object | place | phenomenon
one or more labels (classifications table) with the reason
name, formula or species; provisional name before identification
what the player's own tests found, dated and with the instrument used
the engine's record (CHEMISTRY, ECOLOGY, MEDICINE rows)
where it is found in the world
what it does and what it is used for: on a body (the body docs), in a recipe (GOODS), in a fight (COMBAT)
when it existed (a mineral: always; a species: its era; a compound: made by nature or first made by people)
first obtained pure (oxygen 1774, Scheele and Priestley)
first recognised for what it is (oxygen as an element: Lavoisier 1777)
first made from other things (urea 1828, Wohler)
names; where credit is contested, say so
the in-game date, place, process and apparatus by which the player found or made it; the character who did it
if the game date is before the historical date: 'first recorded <year> by <who>; found here in <game year>: a Time Anomaly'
two columns kept apart: what you found, what the books say

plan.title: The development plan for the universal science engine (phases, sizes, who)
plan.source: ChatGPT's eight priorities (outside AI) sized by the keeper against the belt's capacities (CARD_GAMEDEV, the belt lanes) and the family's existing docs. Research and data tasks are Composer-scale; design decisions are Rex's; nothing is engine code yet.
rows: CHEMISTRY.md reframed: domains, the five separations, 'unknown not impossible', kinetics and equilibrium fields on reactions
